correctness.rationale: Campbell first moment and Poisson isometry prove exact centering and quadratic variation for r>2. At r=2 the exact truncated Lomax second moment yields the log-normalized Brownian clock t/2 and vanishing macroscopic jumps. At 1<r<2 the transformed jump intensity equals y^(-r-1)(1+t^alpha/(beta^(1/r)y))^(-r-1) dt dy, bounded by its limiting stable intensity; finite large-jump convergence plus a uniform Doob small-jump bound proves J1 functional convergence. The self-contained checker passed 271 supporting tests; the analytic arguments prove the infinite claims.

value.rationale: The natural deterministic high-intensity endpoint in a new neutral-occupation limit has a previously unspecified fluctuation law. The exact alpha=1/2 threshold yields all three regimes, exact critical log correction and covariance clocks; above the threshold a nonstationary additive process develops a stable limit with stationary physical-time increments. These are meaningful natural invariants for intermittent clustering, distinct from arbitrary constants or known-table recomputation.
